results.title: Empty script
results.notes: X1: one line, then the script ends; the payload file, the output callback and the broker of one execution
results.methodology: Same-process runs of real plugin engine scripts (docs/memory-phase2/ROADMAP.md T1-T4), the method of the first gate: engines and ScriptRuntime are tracked from EngineLifecycleCallback through weak references, and so are the host-side bridge session objects that BridgeExecutionObserver reports at creation (T1 (a)). After every run the runner collects and polls up to pollMs (1 s once 3 runs stayed reachable); a final collection decides 'retained'. Heap deltas compare the sample after the last warm-up with the final sample; thread, Rhino context, engine and bridge registry deltas compare with the sample before the first run (the plugin probe already bound the plugin), bridge threads with the end of the warm-ups (idle workers of the host's cached binder-call pool get up to 65 s to expire first). Bridge registries must return to the start except the connection pools of the Node, Bun and QuickJS clients, which may keep one idle connection each; system-side connections of this process to the plugin package of the scenario (LoadedApk.mServices, hidden_api_policy 1) may be one above the start. Plugin process PSS is recorded after the second measured run and at the end, never judged (R9); for Bun it includes the bun child processes (same uid). Bun and QuickJS report no session objects yet, so their host-side session classes (broker, output callback, automation bridge, call executor, provider) are counted through VMDebug.countInstancesOfClasses after every run and must return to the count before the first run; their gate lines are read from the global console by a per-run marker. Force mode waits for gateReady(), sleeps forceDelayMs and calls forceStop on every live engine of the run on the main thread.
reasons: retained session instances vs start: bun.broker 22, bun.callback 18, bun.automation 22, bun.callExecutor 22
